questions.q: In a Bicep resource declaration like `resource storageAccount 'Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts@2025-06-01' = { ... }`, what is `storageAccount`?
options: A symbolic name used within the Bicep file to reference this resource — not the actual Azure resource name
The actual name the Azure resource will have once deployed
A required Azure region identifier
The API version being used
questions.explain: The real Azure resource name comes from the `name:` property inside the body, not the symbolic name.

questions.q: What does a Bicep resource compile down to before it's actually deployed?
options: The exact same ARM template JSON — same resource type, same API version, same properties
A completely different deployment format with no relationship to ARM
Bicep resources deploy directly with no compilation step at all
A Terraform HCL file
questions.explain: Bicep is a friendlier authoring syntax over the same underlying ARM deployment engine — nothing about what gets deployed changes.

questions.q: When one Bicep resource's property references another resource's symbolic name, what happens to the dependency?
options: Bicep infers the dependency automatically — no explicit dependsOn needed
The deployment fails unless a dependsOn is written manually
Bicep resources can never reference each other
The dependency must be declared in a separate JSON file
questions.explain: This is one of Bicep's real conveniences over raw ARM JSON, which usually needs an explicit dependsOn spelled out.

questions.q: What does the Bicep Visualizer in VS Code actually show?
options: A live resource-dependency graph generated directly from the open .bicep file — regenerated from the code, never hand-drawn or stale
A static image that must be manually updated when the file changes
A list of every Azure subscription available to the account
A cost estimate for the resources being deployed
questions.explain: Because it's generated directly from the code you're looking at, it can never drift out of sync the way a hand-drawn diagram would.

questions.q: What actually changes between a Bicep resource and its equivalent ARM template JSON, per this lesson?
options: Only how many characters you type and how easy the result is to read — not what gets deployed
Bicep resources deploy faster than ARM JSON resources
ARM JSON supports resource types that Bicep cannot express
Bicep resources cannot use API versioning
questions.explain: Same resource type, same API version, same properties — Bicep only removes ARM JSON's bracketed expression syntax and punctuation.
